statement: Yorùbá oral-historical tradition, as recorded by Samuel Johnson (The History of the Yorubas, completed 1897, published 1921), places Ṣàngó within the Òyó Aláàfin king-list as an early king — though sources disagree on his exact ordinal position (third vs. fourth Aláàfin), which should be reported as varying by source, not as a fixed number. Sàngó in Africa and the African Diaspora (eds. Tishken, Falola, Akinyemi; Indiana UP, 2009), a peer-edited academic volume, is explicitly organized around the mythic-Ṣàngó/historical-Ṣàngó/syncretic-diaspora-traditions split as a central open question, confirming this is real, taken-seriously scholarly territory rather than a popular oversimplification.

sources.citation: Johnson, Samuel. The History of the Yorubas. Ed. Obadiah Johnson, 1921 (completed 1897).
sources.author: Samuel Johnson

sources.citation: Tishken, Joel E., Toyin Falola, and Akintunde Akinyemi, eds. Sàngó in Africa and the African Diaspora. Indiana University Press, 2009.
